Posted February 22, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: Every year the UN narks at the International Narcotic Control Board issue a report demanding that governments take away the freedom of their people. In the past they have even demanded that governments censor anti-prohibitionists, saying that freedom of expression " cannot remain unrestricted when it conflicts with other essential values and rights. "
See
" A Duty To Censor Adults " Ottawa Citizen Editorial Says,
" The whiff of press censorship is unmistakable. "
and links.

It is hard to decide which is more contemptible, the lying UN Narks or the spineless response of the so-called " Justice Minister. " It is quite clear that her commitment to marijuana prohibition overrides her concern for either justice or Canadian sovereignty.

However, this is not playing well in the Canadian press. The ruling Liberal party is in bad odor with the Canadian public for a variety of reasons. The Canadian Press article’s headline immediately below indicates the political nature of all this. " Grit " is the nickname of the Liberals. The second article below is typical of most of the coverage, giving anti-prohibitionist critics plenty of ink, something almost never found in DEAland papers.

It is reassuring that the Canadian courts are not going to go along with this vicious nonsense.)

UN REPORT FUELS GRIT DRUG WAR
By CP
OTTAWA -- Justice Minister Anne McLellan says Ottawa will put more
money into the war on drugs.

She was responding yesterday to a UN report that criticized Canada for being soft on drug crimes.

" It's clear we must do more. That's why we talked in Red Book III and the speech from the throne about the importance of an enhanced drug strategy that deals both with supply and demand. We're going to put more resources toward that. "

The Liberal election platform promised a national drug strategy to reduce the supply of and the demand for drugs, and to crack down on organized crime.

The UN report, released yesterday, said Canadian courts give people convicted of narcotics charges a slap on the wrist. It cited the growing of pot indoors, saying it is especially widespread in B.C., where attitudes toward marijuana are " much more liberal. "
